answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to audit transactions across a multi-agent validation graph. During topological cut verifications, sparse boundaries isolate suspected clusters, slashing stake if consensus contradicts them. Like inspecting a crystal lattice, audits traverse a structured trellis network where a violet indicator flags collusion. Because multi-agent cross-auditing requires controlling cross-cut paths, attacker cost scales with superlinear complexity against honest verification.
